text:
maria: Quick ask — we need a concise enterprise-facing brief (single sheet) that ties together security posture, SLA guarantees, and deployment options. Purpose: hand to AE during inbound qualification and use as a webinar follow-up asset. Draft by EOD Thursday?
aj: OK — can we split: one paragraph on security, one on SLAs, one on deployment modes, plus a short benchmark callout? Keeps it scannable. :+1:
jane: Sounds good. Also we need a routing note: when marketing ops sends an MQL for 'enterprise-security' tag, route to solutions-first AE and create a follow-up task to book the webinar recording.
sam: I'll own the benchmark blurb + a 2-line takeaway about latency/cost tradeoffs across hosted/dedicated/private. Keep numbers conservative and cite internal perf report. Example: "median p50 token latency = 60ms on Dedicated; Hosted typical p50 = 90–120ms with global routing".
lee: For security, call out: VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SOC2/ISO readiness, customer-managed keys. Make it explicit which features map to common procurement questions.
maria: Great. Also need a short webinar script (5 bullets) and 2 CTAs: (1) request a dedicated trial, (2) book a 20-min technical scoping call.
aj: I'll sketch the routing rules for ops: when inbound lead selects "requires SLA" or "enterprise deployment" -> tag as enterprise-sla -> assign to jane, priority = P1. If they select "air-gapped" or "on-prem" add "private-deploy" tag and notify lee.
jane: Can you add checklist items to the brief for AE to use? e.g., 1) confirm data residency, 2) confirm required SLA (latency vs uptime), 3) required compliance standards, 4) deployment preference.
sam: Draft benchmark paragraph (short): "Redwood-tested configs show predictable throughput gains with Dedicated capacity (2–3x token throughput vs single-host hosted bursts) and lower tail latency when KV caching is enabled. Quantization options reduce GPU footprint with modest quality tradeoffs — we recommend 4-bit for pbatch-heavy workloads and int8 for low-latency inference where supported."
maria: Nice. Keep the language non-technical for the brief, technical footnote for the one-pager or appendix. Ops needs a simple copy snippet for the inbound form and for the webinar landing page.
lee: Landing page snippets: 
*Headline:* "Enterprise Inference: Secure, SLA-backed, and deployment-flexible"
*Subhead:* "Choose hosted speed, dedicated predictability, or private control — same API, enterprise controls."
CTA buttons: "Start a Dedicated Trial" and "Request a Technical Scoping Call"
maria: Webinar script bullets (5):
1) 30s intro: what production inference problems we solve.
2) 3min: security & compliance patterns (customer story + features).
3) 4min: SLA & predictable capacity (how Dedicated works + fallbacks).
4) 3min: deployment modes walkthrough (hosted -> dedicated -> private).
5) 2min: next steps + CTAs + Q&A prompt.
aj: For inbound routing copy (short): "Does your deployment need SLAs, private networking, or dedicated capacity? Select all that apply." If any enterprise option selected, append tag: enterprise-high-touch.
jane: AE checklist (short lines to include in the brief):
- Confirm procurement timeline
- Confirm SSO & KMS needs
- Capture required uptime & latency targets
- Note any air-gap/network constraints
- Share benchmark PDF if requested
maria: Can someone assemble the first draft doc + single-page PDF and drop in this thread by Wednesday morning? I want to hand it to growth for landing page copy by Wednesday afternoon.
lee: I can assemble security + deployment sections by Wed AM.
sam: I'll drop the benchmark blurb + one figure (throughput vs mode) by Tue EOD.
aj: Ops snippet and routing rules in a single paragraph by Wed AM.
jane: I'll put together AE checklist + follow-up email template (short) by Wed noon.
ops-bot: Reminder set for 2024-11-20 09:00 to review draft (auto-reminder to participants).
maria: Thanks team. Final ask: keep the brief to a single page (PDF) and include a 2-line technical footnote for AEs. Use plain english, call out next steps clearly. I'll collate and share a final proof before it goes to growth. :sparkles:
